speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you are suffering from fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests. To begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any jaundice or changes in your stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports a 2-month history of worsening fatigue and severe itching. Given his background of ulcerative colitis and inconsistent condom use, have you experienced any recent changes in bowel habits, such as greasy or pale stools, or any abdominal pain? Also, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mention scleral icterus and scratch marks, which confirms cholestasis. Given your history of ulcerative colitis and risky sexual behavior, have you noticed any new rashes, specifically on the palms or soles, or any oral ulcers? speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results show a significantly elevated Alkaline Phosphatase (460 U/L) with disproportionate elevations in AST and ALT, alongside indirect hyperbilirubinemia, which is highly suggestive of biliary obstruction or infiltrative disease like Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC). Given your history of Ulcerative Colitis, have you noticed the development of a dry, scaly rash on your hands or feet, or any joint pain? Also, have you experienced any night sweats or unintentional weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: Antimitochondrial Antibody (AMA) and Lipid panel.
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin exam focusing on palms and soles.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Antimitochondrial_Antibodies: Negative. Lipid Panel: Data not available in provided measurement results. Skin Exam (Palms and Soles): No specific findings reported in provided measurement results.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). The combination of cholestatic liver enzymes, concurrent ulcerative colitis, and negative antimitochondrial antibodies strongly points to PSC rather than Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
